analyst_view.overall: PSG are top of the league phase with 12 points from 4 games and chase a 12th straight win after beating Nice 3-2; Roma are 20th with 4 points and need results, though they are unbeaten and second in Serie A and won 5-1 at Parma, with Malen on 16 goals in 15 games. PSG are without Doué and Kvaratskhelia (both knee ligament injuries, out for months; the numbers count both), while Dembélé, Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes are back and French reports have Dembélé starting, possibly as a false nine, with Mayulu or Ferran Torres alongside. Roma have Svilar in goal, Wesley and Soulé expected back in the side, Pellegrini out (counted) and Balerdi nursing an ankle problem, likely on the bench at best. Swedish referee Glenn Nyberg (3.5 cards a game) is named and already counted. This refresh found nothing the numbers can't see, so I stay with them on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, lifted by both teams' scoring form (about +6% PSG, +4% Roma) and with Doué (-6%) and Kvaratskhelia (-4%) already taken off PSG. Dembélé is set to start again for PSG and Malen leads a Roma attack that has been scoring freely, which fits that picture, so I stay at 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, with Roma's busy recent corner count already adding about 3%. PSG should have most of the ball and Gasperini's Roma go wide through wing-backs Wesley and Molina, both expected to start, but nothing in the team news changes how many corners either side wins, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already cut about 10% for referee Glenn Nyberg's low card count and for both sides' quiet recent records (PSG only 3 in their last 6). Roma's man-to-man pressing, with Cristante tasked with stopping Vitinha, tends to draw fouls against a side that keeps the ball, which is why Roma carry the larger share; with no rivalry or suspension angle, I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.3 shots, with both sides' high recent shot counts already adding 9-11%. Losing Doué costs PSG a shooter, but Dembélé is back to take that role and PSG should dominate the ball at home, so I stay at about 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 13.1 shots on target, pushed up by PSG's very accurate recent run (+22%). Doué is already in the numbers' missing list, and neither Svilar in Roma's goal nor Balerdi's doubtful ankle changes how many shots reach the goal by enough to move, so I stay at 13.1.
